events.query: share of global extreme poor living in FCS economies 2026 compared to 2010

results.text: The global population living in FCS economies more than doubled between 2010 and 2025, rising from 6.0 percent to 13.5 percent. Over this period, a growing number of economies with large populations and high poverty rates became fragile or affected by conflict and violence.10 At the same time, poverty rates fell more rapidly in non-FCS economies, thereby increasing the share of FCS economies in the global total. As of 2026, more than half the extreme poor globally, 57 percent, were living in an FCS economy, up from 12 percent in 2010 (refer to figure 1.11, panel a).

results.text: this is still not the case in the Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan, and Pakistan (MENAAP) region. • Fragility is the defining feature of global poverty. The share of the extreme poor living in a fragile and conflict-affected situation (FCS) rose from 12 percent in 2010 to 57 percent in 2026, as more high-poverty economies became fragile and because extreme poverty fell more quickly in non-FCS economies. By 2030, 87 percent of the extreme poor globally will be living in Sub-Saharan Africa or in an FCS economy or both. • If the per capita economic growth rates observed over 2015–24 persist, the global extreme poverty rate and the number of people living in extreme poverty will increase by 2030: an unprecedented reversal of the decades-long decline. Population growth in high-poverty economies is a key factor in the potential increase.
